screeningScope: Full-text source, eligibility, study-design, taxonomy, and synthesis-readiness review of queue positions 1-12 after Batch 01 publication.

decisionDefinitions.INCLUDE: Eligible for evidence extraction and synthesis after full-text review.
decisionDefinitions.DEGRADED: A required source or verification element was unavailable.

records.sourceFile: Inter-limb asymmetry in youth elite soccer players - Effect of loading conditions.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Fifteen elite youth soccer players completed rear-foot-elevated split squats under three loads and isokinetic knee-flexor and extensor tests. The magnitude and favored side of asymmetry changed across load and test conditions, with only moderate agreement between body-mass and body-mass-plus-25% split-squat conditions.
records.limitations: Small single-academy male sample, cross-sectional laboratory testing, multiple measurement modes, and no prospective injury or performance outcome; the study cannot validate a universal asymmetry threshold.
records.synthesisCaution: Treat asymmetry as test- and load-specific information; do not label an athlete from one percentage or assume the identified side is stable across tasks.

records.sourceFile: Is hip adductor or abductor strength in healthy athletes associated with future groin pain - A systematic review and meta-analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Thirteen prospective cohort studies found a moderate association between lower hip-adductor strength and subsequent groin pain, with low-certainty evidence. Abductor strength and the adductor-to-abductor strength ratio were not associated with future groin pain or time-loss injury.
records.limitations: Strength methods, groin-pain definitions, follow-up timing, and populations varied; only about 3% of the pooled participants were female, and prognostic association does not establish a diagnostic cut point or prevention effect.
records.synthesisCaution: Adductor strength can inform screening and longitudinal assessment, but no single threshold should be presented as a validated prediction rule, especially for female athletes.

records.sourceFile: The effect of fixture congestion on performance during professional male soccer match play - A systematic critical review with meta-analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Sixteen studies examined professional male soccer fixture congestion, defined as successive matches with less than 96 hours of recovery; five studies entered the meta-analysis. Congestion did not materially change total distance, while effects on other physical and technical outcomes were equivocal and tactical evidence was sparse.
records.limitations: Only total distance was measured consistently enough to pool, study quality varied, tactical evidence came from one study, and contextual factors such as rotation, opposition, travel, and match importance were incompletely controlled.
records.synthesisCaution: Stable total distance does not prove complete recovery or unchanged high-intensity, technical, tactical, or individual performance under congestion.

records.sourceFile: The Effect of Training Loads on Performance Measures and Injury Characteristics in Rugby League Players- A Systematic Review.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twelve rugby-league studies suggested that higher training loads could accompany improvements in aerobic power, jumping, and agility while also being associated with more strains, sprains, lower-limb injuries, and overuse problems. The exact dose-response relationship remained inconclusive.
records.limitations: Training-load definitions and measures were inconsistent, designs were observational and heterogeneous, performance and injury outcomes differed, and the review could not identify a transferable optimal or harmful load threshold.
records.synthesisCaution: Do not reduce the findings to 'more load causes injury' or a universal sweet spot; performance adaptation and injury exposure must be interpreted together.

records.sourceFile: Detrimental effects of the off-season in soccer players - A systematic review and meta-analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Across 12 studies, soccer off-seasons involving training cessation worsened body fat, VO2max, intermittent-running performance, jump performance, and repeated-sprint ability. Off-season training programs did not prevent every decline but attenuated losses in VO2max and repeated-sprint ability compared with cessation.
records.limitations: Only healthy male soccer players were included; program content, off-season duration, training status, measurement timing, and study quality varied, with small samples and limited control in several studies.
records.synthesisCaution: Support structured off-season maintenance, but do not prescribe one program or promise complete preservation of fitness from pooled group effects.

records.sourceFile: Adductor strengthening program is successfully adopted but frequently modified in Norwegian male professional soccer teams - A cross-sectional study.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twenty-nine injury-prevention delivery agents from Norway's top two male professional divisions responded to a RE-AIM survey. Awareness and adoption of the Adductor Strengthening Programme were high, but only 10% used the original protocol and 97% planned to continue a commonly modified version.
records.limitations: Self-reported cross-sectional implementation data from one national setting, no independent fidelity observation, no player-level exposure or outcome verification, and no test of whether modified protocols retained the original injury-prevention effect.
records.synthesisCaution: High adoption is not equivalent to protocol fidelity or maintained effectiveness; document modifications and evaluate whether the active dose still matches the intended intervention.

records.sourceFile: Proximal, Distal, and Contralateral Effects of Blood Flow Restriction Training on the Lower Extremities- A Randomized Controlled Tria.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twenty-six healthy adults completed a six-week randomized low-load blood-flow-restriction protocol or control condition. The BFR group improved strength and limb circumference proximal and distal to the cuff, with smaller contralateral gains and no reported adverse events.
records.limitations: Small healthy non-athlete sample, short duration, 16 BFR and 10 control completers, surrogate strength and circumference outcomes, and exclusion of common medical risk groups limit clinical and athlete generalizability and safety conclusions.
records.synthesisCaution: The trial supports a low-load strength stimulus in screened healthy adults, not unsupervised BFR use or proof of safety and efficacy in injured or postoperative athletes.

records.sourceFile: The Adductor Strengthening Programme prevents groin problems among male football players- a cluster-randomised controlled tria.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Thirty-five semiprofessional male football teams were cluster randomized to a progressive Copenhagen-adduction program or normal training. Average weekly groin-problem prevalence was 13.5% in the intervention group versus 21.3% in controls, corresponding to a 41% lower risk of reporting groin problems.
records.limitations: Male semiprofessional football setting, cluster design, self-reported weekly problem surveillance, variable compliance, inability to blind teams, and a nonsignificant effect for substantial groin problems limit transfer to other populations and outcomes.
records.synthesisCaution: Preserve the studied progression and weekly exposure when citing the preventive effect; do not assume an abbreviated or modified Copenhagen protocol has the same result.

records.sourceFile: The effect of cannabidiol on subjective responses to endurance exercise - A randomized controlled trial.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 51 recreationally active adults took 150 mg oral cannabidiol or placebo 90 minutes before a self-paced 10 km run. CBD did not improve affect, enjoyment, motivation, runner's-high features, perceived exertion, pain, or run time.
records.limitations: Young recreational sample, single acute 150 mg dose and product, self-paced outdoor run, subjective primary outcomes, and no elite-athlete, chronic-use, recovery, or therapeutic assessment.
records.synthesisCaution: This null acute trial does not support CBD for improving the subjective endurance experience and does not answer safety, recovery, clinical, or other-dose questions.

records.sourceFile: Acute effects of training loads on muscle damage markers and performance in semi-elite and elite athletes - A systematic review and meta-analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Thirty-two studies showed higher creatine kinase and other indirect muscle-damage signals early in preseason than off-season, little CK change across comparable loads, and concurrent CK changes when training load rose or fell. Other inflammatory and performance responses were inconsistent.
records.limitations: High heterogeneity, group-level pooling, varied sports, age, sex, competition levels, load measures, biomarker timing, and indirect damage markers prevented individual-response conclusions and produced substantial inconsistency in several analyses.
records.synthesisCaution: Creatine kinase is a context-sensitive group signal, not a standalone diagnosis of damage, recovery, or readiness; individual baselines and performance response remain essential.

records.sourceFile: Career outlook and performance of professional athletes after Achilles tendon rupture - A systematic review.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Fifteen studies of professional athletes reported a 76% return-to-play rate and an average 11-month return after Achilles tendon rupture. Returning athletes often had lower efficiency, power, durability, or sport- and position-specific performance than controls.
records.limitations: Retrospective public data dominated, surgical and rehabilitation details varied or were missing, leagues and performance metrics were heterogeneous, female professional evidence was limited, and selection and era effects constrain individual prognosis.
records.synthesisCaution: Use 76% and 11 months as broad professional-sport expectation ranges, not athlete-specific clearance targets or evidence that preinjury performance will be restored.

records.sourceFile: Effects of training and competition on the sleep of elite athletes- a systematic review and meta-analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Fifty-four studies showed that elite athletes frequently missed total-sleep-time or sleep-efficiency recommendations during training and competition. Competition nights averaged about 60 fewer minutes of sleep, while early training, load increases above 25%, difficult travel timing, eastward travel, and altitude were associated with poorer sleep.
records.limitations: Predominantly observational studies, heterogeneous sports and sleep devices, variable recommendation thresholds, limited control of schedule and environment, and group averages that do not define individual sleep need or causality.
records.synthesisCaution: Use schedule and travel factors to protect sleep opportunity, but avoid treating group thresholds or one wearable score as an individual readiness diagnosis.
